subject: Dedicated capacity discovery recap — Aurora Finance
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.inference>
To: Priya Rao <priya.rao@aurorafinance.com>, Evan Liu <evan.liu@aurorafinance.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity discovery recap — Aurora Finance

Hi Priya / Evan,

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciated the clear overview of Aurora's goals. Below is a short recap from our call so we have shared alignment and clear next steps. Please reply with any corrections or additions.

Summary of pain points (what you told us)
- Variable latency and occasional tail spikes on the hosted APIs you currently use; impacts user-facing workflows during batch runs.
- Sensitive billing and customer-identifiable data in prompts; requires stronger data isolation and auditability.
- Current infra is a mix of hosted APIs + a small in-house GPU cluster for experimental models; orchestration/ops cost is growing.
- Need predictable unit economics for forecasting and procurement.

Success criteria for Dedicated fit
- Predictable throughput: steady-state 30 requests/sec with ability to sustain short bursts to 120 req/sec for up to 5 minutes.
- Latency SLOs: 95th percentile < 150ms, 99th percentile < 300ms for your core shorter-chat workloads.
- Data isolation/compliance: tenant isolation at GPU pool level, KMS-backed key control, and audit logs for all inference requests.
- Cost predictability: committed monthly capacity with clear overage/burst policy.
- Operational readiness: autoscaling policy and documented failover to hosted fallback for blackouts.

Current stack & constraints
- Production: Vendor-hosted LLM API for most user features (billing and embeddings).
- Experimental: On-prem single-node GPU runs for sensitive flows.
- Network: All production traffic originates from AWS us-west-2; security team will require egress/IP allowlist details and a minimal set of firewall ports.

Technical notes from the call
- Preferred models: mid-sized dense models (7B–13B) for most features; some higher-capacity generation for summary jobs.
- Typical request sizes: median input ~250 tokens, median generation ~100 tokens.
- KV/cache expectations: long-lived sessions for some users — need KV cache persistence across scaled workers.

Immediate next steps (owner)
1) I’ll follow up with a sizing estimate & pricing range for a Dedicated pool that meets the throughput/latency targets (Aditya) — due EOD Friday.
2) Marissa will draft a mutual action plan and SOW template for a 6–8 week POC (Marissa).
3) Evan / infra to send network and egress IP allowlist + compliance questions (Priya/Evan) — aim for this week.
4) Technical deep dive: Rafael (SE) + Aurora infra team to schedule a 60-minute deep dive next week.

Attachments I’m sharing: Aurora-Dedicated-Requirements.xlsx (brief worksheet to confirm traffic profile), network-reqs-checklist.pdf.

If the recap looks good, I’ll get the sizing + ballpark pricing to you tomorrow and Marissa will circulate the MA Plan. Thanks again — really excited about the possibility of giving Aurora predictable economics and the isolation you need.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Priya Rao <priya.rao@aurorafinance.com>

Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 16:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity discovery recap — Aurora Finance

Thanks Aditya — this is an excellent summary and captures the discussion. A few clarifications / additions: 

- Throughput: the 30 req/sec steady-state is accurate for user-facing production. We also have nightly ingestion jobs that can create spikes; if you can size for 150 req/sec sustained for up to 20 minutes once per night that would be ideal (we can rate-limit).
- Latency: we can tolerate up to 350ms 99th p for the heavier models used in full-document summarization; the 150ms 95th p for chat flows is correct.
- Compliance: we need a signed SSA + proof of audit log retention for at least 13 months.
- Success metrics: 2% or lower error rate for inference failures during the POC, and cost per 1k tokens should be within 15% of our internal target.

Evan will share our network/IP allowlist and a short compliance questionnaire by EOD tomorrow. Also looping in our procurement lead once we have an initial SOW.

Looking forward to the next steps.
—Priya
Priya Rao
VP Product, Aurora Finance
priya.rao@aurorafinance.com
